correctness.rationale: B=M-LZ holds for every percolation realization of any connected unicyclic host. The indicator covariance calculation gives the exact general formula and single-leaf specialization. After odds substitution the polynomial has at most two positive roots by coefficient signs/Descartes. For lengths 3 through 6 a negative-discriminant quadratic dominates it. For L=7 an exact positive rational witness exists; for every L>=8 a uniform analytic positive witness exists. Both endpoints are negative, forcing exactly two distinct simple roots and the full negative-positive-negative phase diagram. A standalone independent-enumeration Python checker passed 212 exact rational assertions. Finite checks support, not replace, the proof.

value.rationale: Two standard network resilience observables—bridges susceptible to single-edge failure, and isolated nodes—show counterintuitive reentrant dependence under bond percolation. Adding just one pendant edge to a cycle replaces a single covariance sign change with a sharply characterized negative-positive-negative pattern, beginning exactly at length seven. The theorem classifies an infinite natural graph family with simple-root guarantees rather than a numerically selected example; it illustrates the competition between retaining new bridges and destroying old cycle bridges.
